abstract: Significance Statement Posttranslational guanidinylation of ApoC3, a major constituent of triglyceride-rich lipoproteins, enhances ApoC3′s proinflammatory properties in uremia. Guanidinylated ApoC3 (gApoC3) is generated by guanidine and urea, and accumulates significantly in the plasma of patients with CKD, and in the kidneys of mouse models of CKD. In humanized mice, gApoC3 promotes kidney tissue fibrosis and suppresses regeneration after vascular injury. Importantly, in a large observational trial examining the clinical relevance of this posttranslational modification in patients with CKD, higher plasma gApoC3 intensity was associated with adverse renal and cardiovascular outcomes. Therefore, gApoC3 represents a novel mediator of kidney injury and CKD-associated vascular disease and offers a potential treatment target to halt progression and to prevent vascular disease in patients with CKD.
